keyVerseText: And the son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian , went out among the children of Israel : and this son of the Israelitish woman and a man of Israel strove together in the camp;
rootMeaning: The term יִשְׂרְאֵלִי (Yisrᵉʼêlîy) is patronymically derived from יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yisrâʼêl), which means 'God prevails.' This root name was first given to Jacob after his wrestling with the angel at Peniel and came to signify not only the individual but also his descendants and the nation that arose from them. Thus, the literal sense of יִשְׂרְאֵלִי points to one who belongs to Israel, carrying the identity of a people marked by God's prevailing power and covenantal relationship.
usageInScripture: The word יִשְׂרְאֵלִי appears twice in Scripture and is consistently translated as 'an Israelite.' It denotes a person who is a descendant or inhabitant of the nation of Israel, emphasizing ethnic and covenantal belonging. This consistent usage highlights the term's role in identifying individuals who are part of God's chosen people, distinguishing them within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יִשְׂרְאֵלִי as 'one belonging to Israel' connects believers to the profound biblical theme of God's prevailing power and faithfulness to His covenant. It underscores the identity of God's people not merely as an ethnic group but as recipients of His promises and participants in His redemptive plan. For the Christian faith, this term reminds us of the continuity between Old Testament Israel and the spiritual Israel, into which believers are grafted by faith in Christ. Recognizing this word's meaning enriches our appreciation of God's sovereign work in history and His call to belong to His covenant community.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 24:10 recounts a conflict involving 'the son of an Israelitish woman,' highlighting the identity of this individual within the community of Israel despite his mixed parentage. The use of יִשְׂרְאֵלִי here emphasizes belonging to Israel and the communal context in which the narrative unfolds. This word draws attention to the complex realities of identity and inclusion within God's covenant people, setting the stage for understanding holiness, justice, and community in the camp of Israel.
